AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: To compare the efficacy, safety and satisfaction from two modes of oral analgesia administration for the treatment of post-caesarean pain in the first 48 h following surgery: on-demand versus fixed time interval administration.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: Open label parallel-group, randomised-controlled trial from February to December 2013.

AbstractText.Label: POPULATION
AbstractText.content: Two-hundred women who underwent caesarean delivery with regional anaesthesia.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Patients were randomly assigned to receive predetermined combinations of tramadol, paracetamol and diclofenac either following patient demand or at predetermined 6-h intervals for the first 48 h. If the patient requested additional analgesia, Percocet (oxycodone and paracetamol) was given as a rescue treatment.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
AbstractText.content: Pain intensity and satisfaction were self-evaluated with visual analogue scale of 0 (no pain/least satisfaction) to 10 (worst pain/highest satisfaction). Breastfeeding, need for supplemental formula, and maternal and neonatal adverse effects were also evaluated.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The 'fixed time interval' group, compared with the 'on-demand' group, had lower mean pain score (2.8 ± 0.84 versus 4.1 ± 0.48, respectively; P < 0.0001), higher satisfaction rate (9.1 ± 1.2 versus 8.3 ± 1.5, respectively; P < 0.0001), more breastfeeds (23.7 ± 6.5 versus 19.2 ± 6.2, respectively; P < 0.0001) and less use of supplemental formulas (8.2 ± 5.2 versus 11.9 ± 6.5, respectively; P < 0.0001). The number of times that drugs were given was slightly higher in the 'fixed time interval' group without an increase in maternal adverse effects, which were mild. No adverse effects were reported for the neonates.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Administration of oral analgesia in fixed time intervals is superior to drug administration following patient demand without increasing maternal or neonatal adverse outcomes.

AbstractText.Label: TWEETABLE ABSTRACT
AbstractText.content: Oral analgesia in fixed time intervals is superior to analgesia following demand.
